Package com.spyj.listener

Class EditorListener

java.lang.Object
com.spyj.listener.EditorListener
public class EditorListener extends Object
Monitors keyboard activity across all BlueJ editor windows by hooking directly into the JavaFX window event system. Records EDITOR_BURST and EDITOR_IDLE telemetry events based on typing patterns.

Because BlueJ does not expose a keystroke-level editor API, this listener attaches a KeyEvent.KEY_PRESSED filter to every JavaFX Stage that matches the BlueJ editor window title format. New windows are discovered automatically via a ListChangeListener on Window.getWindows().

Burst model: consecutive keystrokes in the same editor window form a burst. A burst ends when the user is idle for more than IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS milliseconds, or when focus moves to a different editor stage. Only bursts with at least MIN_BURST_KEYSTROKES keystrokes and a non-zero duration are recorded.

Idle model: a PauseTransition of IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS milliseconds is restarted on every qualifying keystroke. When it fires, the active burst is flushed and the session enters idle state. The idle duration is recorded as an EDITOR_IDLE event when typing resumes or when stop() is called.

All interaction with JavaFX state is performed on the JavaFX Application Thread.

Author:
Mykel Dedier

  • Method Details

    • stop

      public void stop()
      Flushes any in-progress burst and records a final idle event if the session is currently idle. Must be called by SpyJ.terminate() before reading the event store to ensure the final burst and idle event are not missing from the report.

      If called on the JavaFX Application Thread, the flush runs synchronously. Otherwise it is scheduled via Platform.runLater(Runnable) and this method blocks for up to 2 seconds using a CountDownLatch to ensure the flush completes before the caller reads the event store.
